audit.whatIsWrong: Mega Adhesive's GROUNDING is absent from the entire page — all seven phases, both breakdowns, every do and don't. The page names Fling as the matchup-defining cooldown and reduces the glue to scenery ('Get E-flipped into goo' with no explanation). It then repeatedly instructs the player to E-Valor out of the trail, which is exactly the action grounding forbids.
audit.why: Grounding shuts off Broken Wings AND Valor — both of Riven's dashes, her entire escape and her entire engage — for as long as she stands in it. Mega Adhesive is 17s at rank 1, 1000 range, so he throws it from outside every threat range she has. Riot's Fling text also states it explicitly: 'If the target Singed flings lands in his Mega Adhesive, they are also rooted.' Glue-then-fling is a root, not a flip. The mirror reached the same conclusion and recorded the nuance that it only grounds while you are standing in it, so the counterplay is leaving the circle, not dashing out of it.
audit.corrected: Grounding written into content.early, content.mid, whys[3], wants.you[1] and wants.foe[0], with the fling-into-glue root stated from Riven's side exactly as the mirror states it from Singed's.

audit.why: Insanity Potion makes Poison Trail apply Grievous Wounds. While his ultimate is up, standing in the trail cuts YOUR healing — Conqueror, Shieldbow, Death's Dance, all of it. Singed's own sustain is passive regen, not the lifesteal an Executioner's rush answers.
audit.corrected: Stated in content.mid. Did not rewrite report[8].t — it carries encoding damage in the brief and a stale before would drop the whole edit.

edits.before: Your Q resets win level 1 if you weave autos between casts. Identify how Singed contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Level 1 is even: he has a poison toggle and you have no W yet. Take single Q-auto trades and step off the trail instead of trading through it.

edits.before: His move speed and sustain stabilise the lane; don't take bad-angle trades, just maintain CS and watch for fling baits off his proxy trips.
edits.after: Mega Adhesive is 17s at rank 1 and grounds you inside it — stay off the puddle and his fling has nothing to flip you into. That is the whole 4-5 game.

edits.before: At Level 1 he is just a slow melee with a poison toggle — short Q trades are free as long as you walk out of the trail immediately. The danger starts at Level 2: Singed players will intentionally let you start a combo and then E-fling you mid-chain so you land behind him, sprinting deeper into poison. Land your W stun FIRST to lock him in place before committing Q2 and Q3, and the moment the stun ends hit E-Valor to dash out of the trail rather than chasing the kill. He has no way to answer a full Q-W-Q-E-Q sequence if you do not gift him the fling, so Level 3 is genuinely yours.
edits.after: At Level 1 he is just a slow melee with a poison toggle — short Q trades are free as long as you walk out of the trail immediately. The danger starts at Level 2, and it is not the fling: Mega Adhesive grounds you, and grounded means no Broken Wings and no Valor for as long as you stand in it. He drops the glue under you, flings you into it — a landing inside Mega Adhesive roots you outright — then walks off dripping poison. Land W FIRST to lock him before Q2 and Q3, and step off the goo before you spend E, not after. He cannot answer a full Q-W-Q-E-Q if you never stand in the puddle, so Level 3 is genuinely yours.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the slipperiest stretch — his move speed makes it hard to re-engage after a failed trade, and his passive sustain heals back chip damage if you do not commit to a full burst. Keep combo reps clean: bait the fling, side-step or E over it, then go. At Level 6 the lane swings firmly back to you: Blade of the Exile extends your auto-range past his fling hitbox, so you can Q into him, R-empower your next Q3 knockup, and hold Wind Slash for the moment he low enough — the execute scales perfectly with the poison he already dripped on himself. Do not blow Wind Slash early; let his own trail soften him first.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the slipperiest stretch — his move speed makes re-engaging after a failed trade hard, and Noxious Slipstream drafts him off you the moment you turn. Keep combo reps clean: never start a rotation while standing in Mega Adhesive, because grounded means no Broken Wings and no Valor until you leave it. Level 6 swings back to you, but his swings too — Insanity Potion is a flat 100 seconds against your 120 at rank 1, and while it is up his poison applies Grievous Wounds that cut your healing. Blade of the Exile still outranges his 125-range fling, so Q in, R-empower the Q3 knockup, and hold Wind Slash until his own trail has softened him.

edits.before: Use E-Valor to dash out of the poison trail after each combo, not to chase deeper into it
edits.after: Leave the trail with E-Valor before he glues you — Mega Adhesive grounds the dash outright

edits.before: E-fling you behind him so you sprint deeper into his poison trail chasing the kill
edits.after: Glue you first, then fling you into the Mega Adhesive so the landing roots you outright

notes: Mirror reuse: singed__riven had already flipped its chart to the packet's [Skill, Riven, Riven, Skill, Riven, Riven, Skill] and had already established the Mega Adhesive grounding reversal and the 120-vs-100 ultimate gap. I restated both from Riven's side rather than re-deriving them, and flipped the six rows as one atomic group so the two directions match. The single largest defect on this page was that grounding — the mechanic that turns off both of Riven's dashes — appeared nowhere at all, while four separate strings instructed the player to dash out of the exact zone that prevents it.
